title: Pauri 3, sound: gaavai ko taan
hook: gaavai ko taan hovai kisai taan

segments.voice: Yesterday, haumai, the I that fills the picture. Your line was all within the order.

A crowded room, and everyone is singing, but not the same song. One sings about how strong someone is. Another about their generosity. Another about how far away they seem, another about how close. It could be chaos. Instead it sounds like a choir that has agreed on one thing: whoever they're singing about is worth singing about. That's the third pauri of Japji, and its first two words are the whole idea: someone sings.
screen: `A ROOM FULL OF SINGERS.` → `EVERYONE A DIFFERENT SONG.` → `SOMEONE SINGS.`

segments.voice: The opening line: gaavai ko taan, hovai kisai taan. Gaavai: GAA-vai, sings. Ko: short and round, someone. Gaavai ko: someone sings. Taan: a long aa, and the n at the end is made with the tongue curled back a little. It means power, strength. Hovai: HO-vai, if there is, if one has. Kisai: KI-sai, to anyone. Roughly: someone sings of the power, if anyone has the power to sing it. The meaning opens tomorrow. Today, the build. Gaavai ko starts line after line, the way hukmee did in pauri two. Gaavai ko daat jaanai neesaan: someone sings of the gifts. Gaavai ko gun vadiaaeeaa chaar: someone sings of the virtues and the greatness. Gaavai ko, gaavai ko, until the room is full. Some lines swing between opposites: someone sings that He seems far away; someone, that He's right here, face to face. Then the pauri lifts out of the list with a new sound: kathnaa kathee na aavai tot. Kathnaa, kathee: telling, told. There's no end to the telling. Millions and millions tell it, the pauri says, and it never runs out. The last line ends on a word worth listening for, the sound of someone free of every worry: veparvaahu. For now, just the rhythm: gaavai ko, someone sings, voices joining a chorus one by one.
screen: `GAAVAI — SINGS. KO — SOMEONE.` · `TAAN — POWER, STRENGTH.` · `GAAVAI KO, AGAIN AND AGAIN.` · `NO END TO THE TELLING.` · then, large: `PAURI THREE.`

segments.voice: Hum a low note for a breath or two, then put the words on it: gaavai ko taan, hovai kisai taan, and if a tune wants to come, let it; this pauri is about singing. Twice more, slower, then softer. Then stop and listen to the silence after, as if the room of singers has just gone quiet; if you pray, you can rest in Waheguru.
Taan. Power, strength: what someone sings of, gaavai ko taan, line after line in this pauri.
Your line: gaavai ko. Someone sings, and then someone else joins. Day one hundred sixty-seven.

screen: `DAY 167 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: PAURI 3, MEANING: THE CAREFREE ONE.`

howItsDone: The third pauri of Japji is recited each morning; its repeated gaavai ko, someone sings, is often a favorite for learners because the rhythm is easy to catch.

original.script: ਗਾਵੈ ਕੋ ਤਾਣੁ ਹੋਵੈ ਕਿਸੈ ਤਾਣੁ
original.say: GAA-vai ko TAAN, HO-vai KI-sai TAAN
original.note: Gurmukhi: the opening line of Japji's third pauri. the n in taan is retroflex, tongue curled back.

trapdoor: what you thought: a line about singing.
what it means: someone sings of the power, if anyone has the power; the pauri fills with different singers.
what a scholar hears: the final ਣ in taan is a retroflex n; gaavai ko is repeated as an anaphora, like hukmee in pauri two.
